Globally, around 500 million smallholder farmers grow much of the world's food, yet remain largely outside the formal trust infrastructure that lenders, food companies, insurers, certifiers, and government programmes rely on.
Agricultural supply chains already depend on trust, but the trust infrastructure is fragmented.
A lender needs to know whether a farmer exists, what land they farm, what they grow, and whether they have a credible production history.
A food company needs to know where supply comes from and whether it meets quality, sustainability, and compliance requirements.
